body:
[V14 intro](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md) has the following:

> Ensure that a verified application has:
> [...]
> * A secure-by-default configuration, such that administrators and users have to weaken the default security posture.

The part "administrators and users have to weaken the default security posture" reads to me like things get less secure. This seems like an error to me. Is this intentional?

comments.body: I have no idea what this means. Can you submit a PR that removes it?

It does not recommend to make it less secure, but it requires, that things should be by default secure. Not that you need to go through some configuration hardening first.

Personally I prefer it to stay like it is.

"A secure-by-default configuration, such that administrators and users have to weaken the default security posture" is not very clear English. Can we at least expand on this so the sentence fragment makes more sense @Sjord or @elarlang ?

I propose to change this section to the following:

> Ensure that a verified application has:
> 
> * A secure, repeatable, and automated build environment.
> * Dependency and configuration management for third-party libraries, so out-of-date or insecure components are not included by the application.
> * A secure default configuration, suitable for a production system connected to the internet.

> "A secure default configuration"

I think "secure default configuration" is completely different thing than "secure-by-default configuration"

If to think a bit more about it - why I should care at all about default configuration? If I test some application, I should never see default configuration.

Let's say I'm going to test WordPress. What it means, that default configuration must be by secure? If it's changed for production (and this is only thing what matters) - do I need to report, that "yes, in production it's ok BUT by default it was not"? Probably not. 

If you need to go through some security hardening checklist every time, does seem correct either - a bit "product" vs "installation" question.

> "suitable for a production system connected to the internet."

https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md#control-objective

Next line after this 3-item list is:
> Configuration of the application out of the box should be safe to be on the Internet, which means a safe out of the box configuration.

It think this one extra line there duplicates our "problematic line". If I first preferred to keep things like they were, then maybe we just get rid of this line in the list ("A secure-by-default configuration, such that administrators and users have to weaken the default security posture.
").

> Dependency and configuration management for third-party libraries, so out-of-date or insecure components are not included by the application.

Also, this is covered elsewhere.
and current requirement 14.1.3: Verify that server configuration is hardened as per the recommendations of the application server and frameworks in use.

I am dropping "A secure-by-default configuration, such that administrators and users have to weaken the default security posture" for now because it really is confusing. 1e1312c Once we have a better sentence I'll add it back in.

>

>

> ").

Default configuration is often insecure, but not always.

> I propose to change this section to the following:
> 
> > Ensure that a verified application has:
> > 
> > * A secure, repeatable, and automated build environment.
> > * Dependency and configuration management for third-party libraries, so out-of-date or insecure components are not included by the application.
> > * A secure default configuration, suitable for a production system connected to the internet.

Internet or Intranet, it's still a problem. We need to drop "internet" from this.

@elarlang "Configuration of the application out of the box should be safe to be on the Internet, which means a safe out of the box configuration." is problematic for severals reasons as described above. We still need to make this clearer in order to add it back in I state with respect.
